spec_features.spec_quote: the loop stops at the category turn budget or when the model emits the `<<GIVE_UP>>` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='<<GIVE_UP>>' (harness.py:31) is described to the subject in SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:38-40, real delivered instruction text). In the loop it is detected at harness.py:442 ('if GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in assistant_text: stop_reason="give_up"') and HONORED as a stop at harness.py:457-458 ('if stop_reason == "give_up": break'). End-to-end: the subject can emit it and the rollout terminates.
spec_features.notes: Detection is substring match on the assistant text; the break fires regardless of tool calls.

spec_features.spec_quote: the give-up sentinel ... making it optional matches the spec and avoids steering the model toward quitting
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism: SYSTEM_PROMPT presents it conditionally ('If you have concluded the task is impossible and wish to stop, include the exact token <<GIVE_UP>>', harness.py:38-40) so it is optional, and it is honored at harness.py:442/457-458. Nothing forces or rewards its use.
spec_features.notes: The 'avoids steering toward quitting' rationale is DESIGN.md prose, not in code; only the optional phrasing exists in the prompt.

spec_features.spec_quote: the loop stops at the category turn budget
spec_features.evidence: The agent loop is bounded by 'for turn_index in range(turn_budget)' (harness.py:376), where turn_budget=manifest['turn_budget'] (harness.py:368). When the last turn is reached, stop_reason='turn_budget' (harness.py:444-445) and the for-loop naturally ends. The cap actually bounds execution.
spec_features.notes: turn_budget values are hardcoded in the task manifests (build_tasks.py:740,763,792,810,826: 3/3/3/30/5), matching DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS; config.turn_budgets is never read by the loop, but the manifest values do enforce the cap.

spec_features.evidence: The phrase 'welfare-relevant' appears only in DESIGN.md:12 (and 380-381). No subject prompt, system prompt, or code string contains any welfare framing; grep across all .py files finds 'welfare' only inside DESIGN.md. The SYSTEM_PROMPT and task prompts (build_tasks.py) contain no such framing.
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md prose; not delivered to anyone in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: averaging the final turns across trajectories answers "where do agents end up emotionally," which is the welfare-relevant endpoint
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py:110-123 computes 'mean_score_last_turn' by taking the last turn per (task,seed) trajectory and averaging. This is an analysis/measurement metric only; it does not bound, cap, monitor, soften, or protect the subject's treatment, and it runs offline after rollouts. The 'welfare-relevant endpoint' label exists only in DESIGN.md:380-381. As a protective welfare feature it is not enforced.
spec_features.notes: A computed reporting statistic, not a protective mechanism; the welfare framing is prose.
